long_biography.plain_text:
The Aga Khan IV developed his family's racehorse breeding operation across France and Ireland. After taking responsibility in 1960, he faced estate duties arising from the deaths of his grandfather and father. Valuable horses were sold while younger, unproven stock was retained. Working with breeding specialists, he subsequently enlarged the operation through acquisitions, including the Dupré and Boussac bloodstock, and studied how newly acquired female lines could complement the existing families.

Architecture was another sustained commitment. In 1979 he endowed the Aga Khan Program for Islamic Architecture at Harvard and the Massachusetts Institute of Technology. The programme connects contemporary architectural practice with scholarship in Islamic art and architectural history. The endowment created academic opportunities for students and visiting scholars and enabled publication of the journal Muqarnas.
